question.text: Under the Code of Conduct in the Fourth Schedule of SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following is NOT a prescribed obligation of an AIF Manager?

answer.text: Have written policies and procedures to identify, monitor and mitigate conflicts of interest
Operate the fund in the interest of all investors, not just the sponsor or a select class
Guarantee a minimum rate of return to investors via capital-protection mechanisms
Have written policies and procedures to comply with anti-money-laundering laws

explanation.text: The Logic: The Fourth Schedule Code of Conduct requires the AIF and its Manager to operate the fund in the interest of all investors, maintain written conflict-of-interest policies, maintain AML policies, exercise fiduciary conduct, and abstain from assuring returns. The workbook expressly states that the Sponsor and Manager should abstain from assuring returns, so guaranteeing a minimum return contradicts the Code. The Trap: Options A, B, and D are obligations the Code explicitly imposes. Option C contradicts both the Code and the prohibition on assured-return promises. Note: The fiduciary and conflict-policy obligations apply throughout the life of the fund and are tested by SEBI inspections and compliance certifications.
